about: The real clues /learn/ (tools/tutorial.html) teaches each clue type with. Shortlisted by tools/learn_examples.py (our own annotation, device-pure, at most 9 words, no cross-references; ranked by blog-favourite votes and tools/favourite_grading.py surface grades), then read by hand for a surface that is a natural sentence. tests/test_learn_examples.py checks each clue is in its section.

examples.why: Blog favourite, surface graded 5/5. Reads as a plain sentence; a pure two-word anagram with the definition's misleading sense (coins) as the payoff.
Blog favourite, surface 5/5. A natural four-word sentence; fodder is two whole words in clue order, so the letter count check is easy to show.
Best-reading composite in the graded pool (surface 3); reads as a repair story, and the subtract-then-shuffle steps are short: REUNITED minus IT.

examples.clue: Gives the cold shoulder to Italian fellow cycling
examples.why: Reads as a sentence about a snub; one cycle of SIGNORE, the indicator is the word 'cycling' itself.

examples.clue: Dog performing with duck coming last?
examples.why: One of two pure move clues in the pool; the surface (a dog act) is natural and the move is a single letter.

examples.clue: Charm a stubborn person over time
examples.why: Blog favourite, surface 5/5. Three plain pieces (A, MULE, T), shows a down-clue 'over' and a standard abbreviation.
Blog favourite, surface 4/5. A clean one-letter insertion with a vivid, ordinary surface.
Blog favourite, surface 4/5. Three words; teaches the down-clue 'up' the old example taught, without the strained surface.

examples.clue: Student lacks head for income-generating activity
examples.why: Blog favourite. Head deletion of an obvious synonym (LEARNER) and a link word, both easy to see.
Reads as a myth in one line; the L-for-R swap is the commonest substitution and the annotation states it.

examples.clue: On reflection, this sister doesn't change
examples.why: One of two palindromes in the pool; reads as a remark about a nun, with both palindrome indicators.
Blog favourite, surface 5/5. Natural sentence; the answer sits inside one word, so the device is unmissable.

examples.clue: Whisky makers: Ardbeg, Laphroaig and Talisker for starters
examples.why: Blog favourite, surface 5/5. The surface is literally true (they are malt distilleries); four first letters.

examples.clue: Cross and abusive on the phone
examples.why: Surface 4/5; reads as a complaint about a caller. One sound-alike pair (RUDE/ROOD) and a plain indicator.

examples.clue: Spooner's crew decline help with water coming in
examples.why: Surface 3; best-reading spoonerism whose two pieces are both one-step synonyms (BAND, SAG).
Blog favourite. A two-word idiom that splits into two definitions: the cleanest possible double definition.
Blog favourite, surface 4/5. The textbook-quality cryptic definition: two ordinary words, one misleading sense.

examples.clue: A sun proven briefly to be unstable
examples.why: Surface 4/5; reads as an astronomy fact and is an exact anagram (with one cut) as well.
Kept: the graded pool has no clean rebus (its one candidate, V AND A, is a charade). This is the standard textbook rebus.
Short, natural surface; the reverse step is a single anagram (BAD SHAPE = SHAPE rearranged = HEAPS), simpler than the old OUTSTEP.
